questions.stem: You are heading up the Fraser River from the sea. Which side should the red buoys be on?
options: Keep them on your port side
questions.explanation: Red right returning: going upstream, keep red buoys on your starboard side.

questions.stem: What does a starboard-hand buoy look like?
questions.explanation: A starboard-hand buoy is red and conical, with an even number and a red light.

questions.stem: What does a port-hand buoy look like?
questions.explanation: A port-hand buoy is green with a flat top, an odd number and a green light.

questions.stem: You pass buoy 8, then buoy 6, then buoy 4. Which way are you going?
questions.explanation: Numbers get bigger going upstream, so falling numbers mean you are heading downstream or out to sea.

questions.stem: Going downstream toward the sea, which side do you keep the green buoys on?
questions.explanation: Going downstream everything flips. Green buoys, kept to port going upstream, are kept to starboard going downstream.

questions.stem: You see a yellow and black buoy with two black cones, both pointing up. Where is the safe water?
options: Only to the south of it
questions.explanation: Both cones up is a north cardinal. Pass to the north of it.

questions.stem: A buoy is black with a red band and has two black balls on top. What does it mark?
options: A lone danger; safe water all round
The middle of a safe, deep channel
An area where boats are not allowed
A place where you can tie up overnight
questions.explanation: This is an isolated danger buoy. It sits on the danger, so do not pass close to it.

questions.stem: What does a buoy with red and white vertical stripes and a red ball on top tell you?
options: Danger nearby: keep well clear of it
There is safe water all around it
Divers are in the water nearby
questions.explanation: This is a safe water or fairway buoy. It often marks a channel entrance or middle.

questions.stem: Which of these describes a special buoy?
options: Red, with an even number on it
Green, and always numbered in order
Black and red, with two black balls
Yellow; its shape has no meaning
questions.explanation: Special buoys are yellow and, if lighted, show a yellow light. Their shape has no meaning.

questions.stem: On Shuswap Lake you see a white buoy with an orange diamond and a cross inside it. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: An orange diamond with a cross means boats are not allowed in the area. A diamond alone marks a hazard.

questions.stem: What does a white buoy with an orange diamond and no cross mean?
questions.explanation: An orange diamond alone marks a hazard. Words inside may say what the hazard is.

questions.stem: A white buoy has an orange circle with "10" inside. What must you do?
questions.explanation: An orange circle marks a control buoy. The black figure inside is the rule, here a 10 km/h speed limit.

questions.stem: What does a white buoy with an orange square show?
options: A danger such as a shoal
questions.explanation: An orange square gives information, such as directions or services. Swimming buoys are plain white and mark a swimming area.

questions.stem: You see a red triangle sign on a post at the side of a channel. Going upstream, how do you pass it?
options: Keep it on your starboard side
Keep it on your port (left) side
Pass on either side of the sign
Go round it on the north side
questions.explanation: A red triangle is a starboard-hand daybeacon. Like a red buoy, keep it to starboard going upstream. A green square is port-hand.
